nodes.Name: Error
nodes.DocComment:
Error identifies a runtime error used in panic.

The Go runtime triggers panics for a variety of cases, as described by the
Go Language Spec, such as out-of-bounds slice/array access, close of nil
channels, type assertion failures, etc.

When these cases occur, the Go runtime panics with an error that implements
Error. This can be useful when recovering from panics to distinguish between
custom application panics and fundamental runtime panics.

Packages outside of the Go standard library should not implement Error.

nodes.Name: TypeAssertionError
nodes.DocComment: A TypeAssertionError explains a failed type assertion.

Fields.Name: missingMethod
Fields.DocComment: one method needed by Interface, missing from Concrete

nodes.Name: itoa
nodes.DocComment:
itoa converts val to a decimal representation. The result is
written somewhere within buf and the location of the result is returned.
buf must be at least 20 bytes.

go:nosplit

nodes.Name: errorString
nodes.DocComment: An errorString represents a runtime error described by a single string.

Fields.Name: addr
Fields.DocComment: memory address where the error occurred

nodes.Name: Addr
nodes.DocComment:
Addr returns the memory address where a fault occurred.
The address provided is best-effort.
The veracity of the result may depend on the platform.
Errors providing this method will only be returned as
a result of using [runtime/debug.SetPanicOnFault].

nodes.Name: plainError
nodes.DocComment:
plainError represents a runtime error described a string without
the prefix "runtime error: " after invoking errorString.Error().
See Issue #14965.

nodes.Name: boundsError
nodes.DocComment: A boundsError represents an indexing or slicing operation gone wrong.

nodes.Name: boundsErrorFmts
nodes.DocComment:
boundsErrorFmts provide error text for various out-of-bounds panics.
Note: if you change these strings, you should adjust the size of the buffer
in boundsError.Error below as well.
nodes.ValueLiteral: [...]string{abi.BoundsIndex: "index out of range [%x] with length %y", abi.BoundsSliceAlen: "slice bounds out of range [:%x] with length %y", abi.BoundsSliceAcap: "slice bounds out of range [:%x] with capacity %y", abi.BoundsSliceB: "slice bounds out of range [%x:%y]", abi.BoundsSlice3Alen: "slice bounds out of range [::%x] with length %y", abi.BoundsSlice3Acap: "slice bounds out of range [::%x] with capacity %y", abi.BoundsSlice3B: "slice bounds out of range [:%x:%y]", abi.BoundsSlice3C: "slice bounds out of range [%x:%y:]", abi.BoundsConvert: "cannot convert slice with length %y to array or pointer to array with length %x"}

nodes.Name: boundsNegErrorFmts
nodes.DocComment: boundsNegErrorFmts are overriding formats if x is negative. In this case there's no need to report y.

nodes.Name: printpanicval
nodes.DocComment:
printpanicval prints an argument passed to panic.
If panic is called with a value that has a String or Error method,
it has already been converted into a string by preprintpanics.

To ensure that the traceback can be unambiguously parsed even when
the panic value contains "\ngoroutine" and other stack-like
strings, newlines in the string representation of v are replaced by
"\n\t".

nodes.Name: printanycustomtype
nodes.DocComment: Invariant: each newline in the string representation is followed by a tab.

nodes.Name: panicwrap
nodes.DocComment:
panicwrap generates a panic for a call to a wrapped value method
with a nil pointer receiver.

It is called from the generated wrapper code.
